title: Counting expressions: singular noun
focus: In basic counting phrases, numbers greater than one and monta take a singular partitive noun: kaksi kirjaa — two books.

exercises.explanation: After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Counting expressions: singular noun: form or use confused

optionFeedback.kirjaa: After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.
optionFeedback.kirja: kirja is not the required partitive form for this meaning. After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.
optionFeedback.kirjoja: kirjoja does not express the requested case and number here. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.
